Franklin W. Dixon, The Tower Treasure.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/franklin-w-dixon/the-tower-treasure

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Franklin W. Dixon, the author named on the book, no death year recorded (Wikidata Q369206). Franklin W. Dixon is a pen name (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tower_Treasure); the ghostwriters who wrote the text are not named in the facts.

First publication of the text used: 1927 (SE colophon: 'The Tower Treasure was published in 1927 by Franklin W. Dixon.'; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tower_Treasure lists the United States as the country and Grosset & Dunlap as the publisher).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1927, before 1931. A work published in 1927 entered the United States public domain on 1 January 2023. Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published there, so the US rule settles the origin whatever the death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'The Tower Treasure was published in 1927 by Franklin W. Dixon.'
- Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tower_Treasure (country United States, publisher Grosset & Dunlap)
